newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO ministers set to order new force into Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO ministers set to order new force into Bosnia.

text.p: NATO defence ministers were set on Tuesday to order a new alliance-led peace force into Bosnia to police the Dayton peace accords when the mandate of the current force expires on December 20.

The 16 ministers, meeting in Brussels to discuss reform of the alliance and relations with Russia, were expected to issue an "ACT-ORD" (order to act) to the new force later in the day so commanders could begin deployment ahead of the transfer date.
NATO foreign ministers last week formally agreed to send a 25,000-30,000-strong force to Bosnia for a further 18 months to police the peace accords which ended the 3-1/2 year war in November 1995.
The new Stabilisation Force (SFOR), which takes over from an Implementation Force (IFOR) double its size, was endorsed by the U.N. Security Council.
Russia and some 16 other non-alliance nations, which also took part in IFOR, have agreed to stay on and participate in SFOR.

"There is no contentious or controversial issue for us to discuss in Bosnia...Tomorrow, the NATO defence ministers, I predict, will unanimously issue the order for SFOR," U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry told reporters on Monday.

The ministers, who will be joined on Wednesday by Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, will spend much of the two-day meeting reviewing attempts to bring the alliance more into line with the reality of the post-Cold War security situation.
They are hoping Russia will agree to build on cooperation achieved during the planning for SFOR by exchanging military liasion officers between the political and military commands of NATO and Moscow.

Perry said on Monday that broad U.S.-French relations had not been soured by a bitter dispute over NATO reorganisation, but insisted Washington would not bow to French demands to give up command of the alliance's southern flank.

"It is not an issue which has soured or affected our other relations with the French," Perry said. "It is not a personal issue. I still have excellent working and personal relationships with Minister Millon. I expect to meet and talk with him in the next day or two."
France is demanding that Washington surrender that traditional U.S. post to a European officer as part of reforms to give Europeans a bigger say in the traditionally U.S.-dominated alliance.
